identifiers.identifier_scope: Identifiers correspond to the small-molecule nucleoside analog 8-chloroadenosine.

drug_class: Purine nucleoside analog; investigational antineoplastic agent

mechanism_of_action.plain_language: 8-Chloroadenosine is an investigational adenosine analog that enters cells and is phosphorylated to 8-chloro-ATP. This metabolite depletes endogenous ATP pools, interferes with RNA synthesis and polyadenylation, activates cellular energy-stress signaling, and can induce apoptosis in malignant cells.
mechanism_of_action.molecular_action: Intracellular conversion to 8-chloro-ATP leads to inhibition of RNA synthesis/transcriptional processes and bioenergetic stress with AMPK pathway activation. The agent is not established as a selective inhibitor of a single canonical protein target.
mechanism_of_action.selectivity: Non-selective nucleoside analog mechanism; no single validated primary protein target established in humans.

typical_use.cancer: Hematologic malignancies and selected advanced solid tumors
typical_use.histology: Primarily acute myeloid leukemia and multiple myeloma in early clinical investigation
typical_use.scope: Investigational use only; not approved for routine oncology care.

potential_repurposed_uses.proposed_rationale: Preclinical and early clinical work suggests leukemia cells may be vulnerable to ATP depletion and transcriptional inhibition caused by intracellular 8-chloro-ATP accumulation.
potential_repurposed_uses.human_evidence: Phase I experience has been reported in relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia.

potential_repurposed_uses.proposed_rationale: Myeloma cells may be sensitive to transcriptional stress and energy depletion induced by 8-chloroadenosine.
potential_repurposed_uses.human_evidence: Phase I testing has been reported in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.
limitations: No confirmed objective response benchmark suitable for routine use

adverse_effects.biological_explanation: May relate to systemic energy depletion and cytotoxic stress.
Common nonspecific toxicity with intravenous cytotoxic investigational agents.
Possible injury to rapidly proliferating gastrointestinal mucosa.
Cytotoxic effects on marrow progenitors may occur, although attribution can be confounded by underlying hematologic malignancy.

other_reported_adverse_effects.biological_explanation: Nonspecific systemic and gastrointestinal toxicity profile reported in early-phase studies.
